new_task_1.title: Preserve lazy execution when converting datasets to dask dataframes
new_task_1.description: The upgrade adjusts `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` so non-dask variables are chunked before they are broadcast across multiple dimensions. This avoids eager expansion into oversized in-memory arrays and keeps dataframe conversion viable for large multidimensional datasets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that converting a dataset to a dask dataframe does not eagerly materialize large NumPy arrays when a variable must be broadcast over several dimensions during conversion.

expectation.grounded: Within `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()`, variables that are not already backed by dask must be converted to dask-backed arrays before `set_dims(ordered_dims)` and dataframe construction proceed. The conversion path must then continue through dask-based reshaping and `dd.from_array(...)` so that broadcasting a variable to the dataset's ordered dimensions remains lazy rather than creating a large in-memory array first.
expectation.conceptual: Dask dataframe conversion should preserve lazy execution even when dataset variables need dimensional broadcasting. Users should be able to convert large datasets without the conversion step unexpectedly expanding NumPy-backed variables in memory.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to the `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` conversion path. Variables that are already dask-backed should continue through the existing path unchanged, while non-dask variables should be chunked before broadcasting. The resulting dataframe construction should still use the dataset chunking layout and existing column-generation behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should address memory blowups caused by eager broadcast, not change the dataframe's logical contents or require callers to pre-chunk their datasets manually.

behavior: `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` now coerces non-dask variables to dask arrays before broadcasting them to the full ordered dimension set.
Broadcasting multidimensional variables during dask dataframe conversion remains lazy instead of expanding an in-memory NumPy array first.
Large dataset conversion scenarios that previously risked oversized intermediate arrays can proceed through the dask-backed conversion path.
Variables already backed by dask continue to use the existing lazy dataframe-construction flow.
acceptance_criteria: When `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` is called on a dataset containing a non-dask variable that must be broadcast across multiple dimensions, the conversion should avoid eager full-size materialization of that broadcasted array.

When the same conversion is performed on a large dataset, the method should remain on a dask-backed execution path through dataframe creation rather than failing because broadcasting produced an oversized in-memory array.
When a variable is already backed by dask, `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` should continue to convert it without changing the intended lazy dataframe output behavior.
The logical dataframe contents and column construction should remain consistent with the pre-existing `to_dask_dataframe()` API apart from the avoided eager-memory blowup.
